```{r, include = FALSE}
# Executed chunks are wrapped so the site can run them in the browser with webR.
knitr::knit_hooks$set(webr = function(before, options) if (before) "\n<div class=\"webr-chunk\">\n" else "\n</div>\n")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", webr = TRUE)
```

```{r}
library(REDCapCDMSTAT)
nx <- cdmstat_demo(dir = file.path(tempdir(), "dm"), reset = TRUE, actor = "dana")
```

All state lives in one SQLite **ledger** next to the cache, so the R
package, the Shiny app, the web app and reports all see the same queries,
locks and signatures. Every action is recorded in an append-only activity
trail (`nx$activity()`).

## Validation rules

Four rule families come from the data dictionary itself, so they follow the
dictionary when it changes:

| Rule | Finds |
|---|---|
| `range:` | values outside the field's validation min/max (numbers and dates) |
| `required:` | required fields left empty on a form that has data |
| `branching:` | values recorded in a field that branching logic hides |
| `calc:` | stored calculated fields that differ from a recalculation |

```{r}
nx$validate()[, c("rule", "record_id", "event", "value", "message")]
```

Custom rules use REDCap logic syntax, including cross-event references such
as `[baseline_arm_1][weight]`:

```{r}
nx$add_rule("weight_change", "abs([weight] - [baseline_arm_1][weight]) < 15",
            "Weight changed by 15 kg or more since baseline", "warning", field = "weight")
nx$validate()[startsWith(nx$validate()$rule, "custom:weight"), c("record_id", "event", "value")]
```

## Queries

```{r}
nx$raise_queries()
q <- nx$queries()
id <- q$query_id[q$record_id == "15"]
nx$transition_query(id, "answered", "Site: transcription error, correct value is 130", actor = "site_crc")
nx$transition_query(id, "resolved", "Verified against the source document", actor = "dana")
nx$query_audit(id)[, c("action", "actor", "old_status", "new_status", "comment")]
```

Transitions follow `open → answered → resolved → closed`, with reopening
allowed, and each needs a reason. With the
[DRW External Module](drw-module.html), queries also appear in REDCap's Data
Resolution Workflow, and site replies made there flow back.

## Randomisation

A stratified, permuted-block schedule is generated once and concealed.
Each subject gets exactly one allocation, and the arm is written to the EDC:

```{r}
nx$setup_randomization(strata = c("site", "sex"), block_sizes = c(4, 6), per_stratum = 60, seed = 2026)
nx$backend$add_record("121", list(consent_date = "2025-12-02", dob = "1984-06-01", sex = "2", site = "3",
                                  enrollment_complete = "2"))
nx$sync()
str(nx$randomize("121", actor = "peter")[c("record_id", "stratum", "seq", "arm_label", "written_to_edc")])
try(nx$randomize("121"))
```

## Source data verification (SDV)

A risk-based plan verifies forms with critical fields at 100%, plus the first
*N* subjects at each site and a random sample of the rest. When a verified
form is edited, it goes back to *reverify*:

```{r}
s <- nx$sdv_plan(critical_fields = c("arm", "event_occurred", "ae_serious"), first_n = 2, sample_rate = 0.1)
table(required = s$required)
k <- "1|baseline_arm_1|vitals|"
nx$sdv_verify(k, actor = "mona")
nx$backend$edit("1", "sbp", "101")
nx$sync()
nx$sdv_status()[nx$sdv_status()$unit_key == k, c("unit_key", "status", "verified_by")]
```

## Locks and electronic signatures

```{r}
lk <- nx$lock("10", "Interim database lock")
sig <- nx$esign("10", "I approve the data of this record as Principal Investigator",
                actor = "peter", identity_verified = TRUE)
nx$backend$edit("10", "weight", "70.1")
nx$sync()
nx$locks()[, c("record_id", "reason", "integrity")]
nx$signatures()[, c("record_id", "signer", "status")]
```

A signature binds the signer, its meaning and a hash of the record's data. In
the web app the signer must re-enter their key, and the gateway checks it
before signing. With the External Module, `lock()` also locks the forms
inside REDCap, so REDCap itself refuses edits.

## Medical coding

```{r}
nx$code_terms("ae_term")
cd <- nx$coding()
cd[!duplicated(cd$verbatim), c("verbatim", "status", "term", "suggestion_term", "score")]
```

Exact and synonym matches are auto-coded, and near misses wait for a coder
(`nx$approve_coding()`). The bundled dictionary is a demo with fictitious
codes; load your licensed MedDRA or WHODrug export with
`nx$load_dictionary("meddra_llt.csv")`.

## Protocol deviations

```{r}
nx$check_visit_windows(window = 7)
nx$deviations()[, c("record_id", "event", "category", "description", "severity")]
```

## Site metrics

```{r}
nx$site_metrics()[, c("site", "subjects", "open_queries", "rule_violations", "sdv_required", "sdv_verified_pct", "deviations")]
```

For several studies at once, `cdmstat_portfolio()` and `run_portfolio()`
summarise each study and their sites side by side.
